title: Plan the whole cluster before splitting it
statement: Plan a sequence or group of related knowledge as a whole, with one target performance, a throughline and a persistent example, before splitting it.
detail: The reading project's alignment plan makes the cluster (one named performance, 1–2 knowledge types, 2–5 KCs, one load-bearing throughline) the unit of design, generation and reteaching, and generates the cluster's reasoning before decomposing it into knowledge components and then items (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/academics-alignment-plan.md`). It records the round-2 sequencing finding that atomising first on narrative subjects produced "locally-correct micro-lessons that never cohere". The curriculum BrainLift gives the upper limit: as the surface area of the task grows, the precision and discipline of a model's output degrade (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback1/Curriculum & Knowledge BrainLift.md`). Keep each generated unit to one performance.
against: The curriculum BrainLift says this matters little for modular, abstract material such as much of maths, where atomising first is close to lossless (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback1/Curriculum & Knowledge BrainLift.md`, line 538). The finding is stated for narrative subjects (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/academics-alignment-plan.md`).
